entries.title: The Effect of Health Insurance on Crime: Evidence from the Affordable Care Act Medicaid Expansion
entries.key_finding: Quasi-experimental (DiD) test of Medicaid expansion on county-level crime: insurance coverage as crime-reducing treatment - the direct causal bridge exists in econ working-paper form.

entries.title: The Effect of Medicaid on Crime: Evidence from the Oregon Health Insurance Experiment
entries.key_finding: Uses the OREGON RCT (the strongest health-insurance identification anywhere) for a crime outcome - Medicaid coverage's causal effect on criminal-justice exposure. This is the cleanest insurance->crime causal test found.
entries.design: Lottery-based RCT spillover to crime outcomes

entries.title: Medicaid Expansion and Crime Outcomes
entries.key_finding: Peer-reviewed journal article estimating Medicaid expansion -> crime outcomes - the causal bridge has crossed into a peer-reviewed economics journal.

entries.title: Medicaid Expansion, Ride-sharing and Crime: Evidence from US Cities
entries.key_finding: Adds a second mediating mechanism (ride-sharing access) between expansion and city-level crime - mechanism-composition inside the insurance-crime causal chain.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (mechanism decomposition on the insurance->crime chain)

entries.title: The Effect of Substance Use Disorder Treatment Use on Crime: Evidence from Public Insurance Expansions
entries.key_finding: Public-insurance expansions raise SUD-treatment take-up and LOWER crime - the harm-reduction mechanism inside the insurance-crime causal chain (treatment-access channel).
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (mechanism: treatment access reduces criminal exposure)

entries.title: Is the Affordable Care Act Medicaid Expansion Associated With Reported Incidents of Child Sexual Abuse?
entries.key_finding: Medicaid expansion associated with reduced reported child sexual abuse - extends 'crime' to child-maltreatment outcomes; abstract frames ACA access as mitigating risk factors for maltreatment.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (maltreatment endpoint on the insurance-crime arc)

entries.title: County-Level Medical Debt and Its Associations With Cancer Stage and Survival in the United States
entries.key_finding: County-level medical debt in collections as ECOLOGICAL predictor of cancer stage at diagnosis and survival - the debt-as-county-exposure design exists but points at cancer, not crime. Closest analog to the founder's county debt -> county crime design; crime endpoint not used.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (county debt ecological design VERIFIED; no crime outcome)

entries.title: Medical Financial Burdens and Later Risks of Adult Psychological Distress (2014-2023)
entries.key_finding: Temporal ordering established: medical financial burdens at t predict adult psychological distress at t+1 - the stress-pathway from medical debt to mental-health harm measured longitudinally.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (medical debt -> psychological distress, longitudinal order)

entries.title: Medical Debt and Deferred Care for Physical Health, Mental Health, and Dental Needs Among U.S. Adults
entries.key_finding: Medical-debt burden predicts deferred care across physical/mental/dental need - harm-accumulation via care-avoidance (the deprivation channel of the debt-harm chain).

entries.title: Association of Medical Financial Hardship and Mortality Risk among US Adults
entries.key_finding: Medical financial hardship associated with elevated all-cause mortality risk in US adults - the harm extreme of the debt-harm chain.

entries.title: Association of Medical Financial Hardship and Mortality Among Cancer Survivors in the United States
entries.venue: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
entries.key_finding: Long-term health consequence measurement: financial hardship elevates mortality among cancer survivors - hardship as independent mortality risk factor.

entries.title: Losing Ground: Racial Disparities in Medical Debt and Home Foreclosure in the Deep South
entries.key_finding: Medical debt predicts home foreclosure; racial disparities concentrated - debt cascades to housing instability (hardship-continuum evidence).

entries.title: Understanding the Aggressive Practices of Nonprofit Hospitals in Pursuit of Patient Debt
entries.key_finding: Documents aggressive hospital-side collection practices against patients persisting post-ACA - the creditor-side behavior of the debt system (collection aggression canon, no violence endpoint).

entries.title: Identification With a Violent and Sadistic Aggressor: A Rorschach Study of Criminal Debt Collectors
entries.key_finding: 27 criminally-convicted debt collectors psychologically profiled (Rorschach) - collector-side violence exists in the literature as PERSONALITY pathology, not as an ecological debt-to-violence channel.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (collections-violence thread exists only at perpetrator-psychology grain, no population/ecological design, no medical-debt specificity)

entries.title: Incapacitating Debt: Investigating the Community-Wide Effects of Incarceration on Medical Debt
entries.key_finding: Runs the arrow IN REVERSE: incarceration as cause, community medical debt as outcome - the crime-to-debt direction exists; the debt-to-crime direction at the county level does not.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (reverse-causality direction indexed; highlights absent forward direction)

entries.title: Commercial Health Care Prices and Medical Debt in the US
entries.key_finding: Treats medical debt as a downstream of PRICING (commercial price variation predicts debt burden) - structural upstream framing of the debt burden; no crime/behavioral endpoint.

entries.title: The Oregon Health Insurance Experiment: Evidence from the First Year
entries.key_finding: The foundational RCT: Medicaid reduces financial strain, collections and out-of-pocket debt - the treatment side of the debt-crime channel without testing crime itself.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (insurance reduces the debt burden - the treatment arm)
entries.url: PMID 23293397 (secondhand-tagged: EPMC abstract pull failed twice)

entries.title: Health insurance, medical debt, and financial well-being
entries.key_finding: Two natural experiments (ACA under-26 provision; Medicare eligibility) show insurance measurably reduces medical debt and lifts financial well-being - insurance as treatment against the debt burden.

entries.title: Medical Debt and Advanced Cancer Stage at Diagnosis
entries.key_finding: Personal-level medical-debt burden associated with more advanced cancer at diagnosis and higher mortality - harm-channel replication at individual grain.

entries.title: Medical debt and subsequent use of alternative financial services among US adults
entries.key_finding: Medical debt pushes households toward payday/alternative financial services - the downstream-cascades behavior evidence (predatory-finance exposure, adjacent to the crime endpoint via victimization-prone credit channels).
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (behavioral cascade documented; no crime endpoint)

entries.title: Changes In Medical Debt And Bankruptcy After Acute Traumatic Injuries, 2019-21
entries.key_finding: Post-ACA, acute-injury debt and bankruptcy persists - debt burden insensitive to insurance expansion among acute events (limits the insurance-as-remedy claim; ties the debt and insurance strands).

entries.title: Increased Medical Debt in Collections 1 Year After Emergency General Surgery Admission
entries.key_finding: Acute surgical admission produces collections-debt one year later - debt-in-collections as a measurable exposure variable (confirms county collections data are real-exposure, not just billing noise).
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (exposure-validity support for the county-collections data lane)

entries.title: Housing Instability Following Medical Debt Exposure Among US Adults, 2023 to 2025
entries.key_finding: Medical-debt exposure precedes housing instability (2023-25 adult panel) - hardship-cascade canon continues; housing instability is itself a crime-correlated exposure (untested mediation).
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (cascade step measured; crime mediation absent)

summary: Novelty verdict summary (SCAN-14, HEALTHCARE-DEBT vs CRIME): The INSURANCE->CRIME causal direction is small-but-real and now VERIFIED across designs (SSRN 2017 DiD; Oregon-RCT 2024; Atlantic Economic Journal 2025; ride-sharing mediation 2025; SUD-treatment mechanism 2014; child-maltreatment extension PMID 35213252) - health coverage measurably reduces crime at county/city level. What is ABSENT everywhere: no study in the retrieved corpus links MEDICAL DEBT (the debt-in-collections channel, county-level) to CRIME as an outcome - the county-debt ecological design exists and points at cancer/mortality/housing (PMID 42612687; 35442439; 41525068), the collection-aggression literature exists but stays institutional/perpetrator-side (PMID 34893829; 26226052, Rorschach n=27), and the ONE crime-adjacent debt study runs the arrow in reverse (incarceration -> medical debt, Crime & Delinquency 2026). => Founder's one-pager-#4 slot is a real NOVEL-ANGLE (leaning GAP): insurance->crime = VERIFIED, medical-debt->crime = GAP. Bridge design (county debt-in-collections -> county violent-crime, lagged, from the collections data the 2026 cancer-survival papers validate) appears unoccupied.
source_routes: EuropePMC (resultType=core) + PubMed esearch/efetch + keyless Crossref (api.crossref.org); EPMC 503s on first pass, retried via PMID EXT_ID pulls
abstract_policy: Every entry's abstract loaded first-hand via EPMC resultType=core unless tagged secondhand; effect sizes only where stated in loaded abstract.
